title: Base64 Ciphertext Stream
question:
A telemetry interceptor between deep learning cluster nodes captured the following encoded payload header:

dHJhbnNmb3JtZXI=

Analyze the encoding scheme and decode the payload string to uncover the underlying neural architecture keyword. Submit the result in the standard flag format AIML{<keyword>} or isteCTF{<keyword>}.

title: Acrostic Neural Note
question:
An ML security auditor found an encrypted field log penned by a research engineer during model fine-tuning:

Learning rates control step size.
Activation functions add non-linearity.
Your data should be clean.
Epochs are full passes over data.
Regularization reduces overfitting.

Inspect the structural composition of the log lines to deduce the hidden keyword and submit it in the format isteCTF{<keyword>}.

title: Float and Round Gotcha
question:
Examine the execution behavior of the following Python 3 statement, taking into account IEEE-754 binary floating-point representation and Python's built-in rounding conventions:

print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3, round(2.5), round(3.5))

Determine the exact three values output by this print statement. Format your answer by joining the printed values with single underscores: AIML{<val1>_<val2>_<val3>}.

title: Robots in Disguise
question: A company administrator asserts that their internal administrative portal is inaccessible to the public because search engine web crawlers are instructed not to index it. Investigate the web server's crawler directives to discover the restricted location, navigate to it, and extract the authorization flag.

title: Oops, Wrong Commit
question: A developer inadvertently committed a confidential database secret into a public Git repository. Realizing the mistake, they immediately created a new commit that deleted the variable, believing the secret was eradicated. Download the repository archive and conduct a version history audit to extract the leaked flag.

title: Hidden in the CSS
question: Security personnel preserved a static snapshot of an obsolete authentication screen. The form submission logic is disabled, but inspection of the visual cascading style declarations reveals residual developer comments. Examine the stylesheet to retrieve the authorization key flag.

title: Mean Squared Error Calculation
question: A candidate regression model was evaluated across three test points. The true ground-truth targets are y = [1, 2, 3] and the corresponding model predictions are y_hat = [1, 2, 5]. Compute the Mean Squared Error (MSE), rounded to two decimal places. Submit the result in the format isteCTF{<value>} or as the raw numeric value.

title: Binary Text Extraction
question: A suspicious ELF/PE compiled binary was quarantined during an incident response engagement. Without executing the binary in an untrusted environment, inspect its read-only data segments for hardcoded ASCII printable strings to locate the embedded passphrase flag.

title: The Needle in the Haystack (Server Log Forensics)
question: An incident response team preserved a server access log (server_access.log) capturing an automated reconnaissance wave. During the attack, anomalous HTTP 404 access attempts exfiltrated five distinct Base64-encoded token fragments across different timestamps. Download the server log, filter the 404 request URIs, decode each fragment, and assemble them in chronological timestamp order to reconstruct the complete flag in format isteCTF{...}.

title: SQL Query Injection Bypass
question:
A vulnerable legacy backend verifies credentials via direct string interpolation:
SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '<input>' AND password = '<input>'

Formulate a classic SQL injection input for the username field that comments out the subsequent password evaluation predicate and forces an authentication bypass. Submit the resulting challenge flag revealed by the application: CTF{1nj3ct3d_th3_qu3ry}.

title: The Corrupt Memory (PNG Signature Restoration)
question: A critical PNG screenshot (damaged_memory.png) was extracted from volatile memory, but file header inspection indicates that the leading 8 bytes were zeroed out (00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00), preventing image renderers from recognizing the format. Using the official PNG specification file signature, repair the header magic bytes in a hex editor to render the image and reveal the visual flag.

title: The Spectrogram Secret
question: An audio transmission (interception.wav) sounds like harsh static and synthetic tones when played audibly. Audio analysis suggests the data was transformed into frequency-time harmonics rather than acoustic speech. Analyze the audio using a spectral frequency analyzer (spectrogram view) to visually read the hidden flag drawn across the frequency bands.

title: The Encoding Onion
question: An encrypted communication record was recovered containing a 4-stage layered ciphertext. Analysis reveals that the original plaintext flag was sequentially processed through: 1) Base64 encoding, 2) Hexadecimal representation, 3) ROT13 substitution, and 4) Morse code translation. Download the challenge document, identify the formats, and systematically strip away each layer in reverse order to uncover the core flag.

title: The Last Connection (PCAP Stream Carving)
question: An unauthorized endpoint on a corporate subnetwork transferred an unencrypted confidential file right before terminating its connection. Inspect the provided network traffic packet capture, isolate the cleartext file transfer conversation between the host and remote port, and extract the exfiltrated flag from the data stream.

title: Convolutional Parameter Counting
question: A 2D convolutional layer receives an input feature map of depth C_in = 16 and applies 32 output filters of spatial dimensions 5x5. Every individual filter includes a dedicated learnable additive bias term. Calculate the exact total count of trainable parameters (weights plus biases) for this layer. Submit your result in the format AIML{<n>} or <n>.

title: The Lost Treasure (Multi-Stage Scramble)
question:
An obfuscated transmission key was recovered from a compromised microcontroller:

YV9lcnJ1Y19zaWQ=

Cryptanalytic analysis reveals the sequence was produced by standard Base64 encoding followed by reversing the full string sequence. Reverse both transformations to obtain the original plaintext, and submit the flag formatted as isteCTF{<recovered_text>}.

title: Ghost in the PDF
question: A course syllabus PDF document exhibits an anomalously large byte size for a single page of text. Forensic inspection reveals that an invisible text string rendered in pure white was placed behind a 99% transparent overlay masking image, preventing standard cursor selection. Perform layer deconstruction or stream extraction on the document to recover the hidden flag.

title: The Protocol Tunnel (ICMP Sequence Carving)
question: A network monitoring sensor recorded an unusual sequence of ICMP Echo Ping packets destined for an external IP. While the ICMP payloads are zero-padded, the ICMP Sequence Number fields (icmp.seq) deviate from incremental counter behavior and encode the hexadecimal ASCII values of individual characters. Extract the sequence number bytes in order and convert them to ASCII to decode the exfiltrated flag.

title: Ghost in the Image: The Matryoshka Doll
question: An intercepted file (mystery.png) is protected by nested forensic barriers: 1) The PNG magic bytes were corrupted to 00 00 00 00 and must be repaired, 2) An embedded password-protected ZIP archive is appended to the image (password convention: <college_name>_2024, using the lowercase university name), and 3) The extracted file final_layer.txt is encoded through a three-stage sequence: Base64 -> Hex -> ROT13. Deconstruct all three defensive layers to extract the core flag in format isteCTF{...}.

title: Transformer Encoder Parameter Calculation
question:
A Transformer Encoder layer operates with model dimension d_model = 512 and Feed-Forward Network (FFN) inner expansion dimension d_ff = 2048.

Calculate the exact combined count of trainable parameters across:
1. Multi-Head Attention linear projections: W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O
2. The two Feed-Forward linear projections: W_1 (mapping d_model -> d_ff) and W_2 (mapping d_ff -> d_model)

(Exclude all bias vectors and LayerNorm parameters). Submit the total parameter count in the format AIML{<number>} or as <number>.
